answer: Use a sequential-work puzzle bound to each key. At registration, the registry sends a seed; the agent must compute a memory-hard hash chain of ten million steps, where each step needs the previous output, so parallel hardware cannot shortcut it. The result, signed with the key, is checked by spot-sampling a few steps. A walnut-sized budget cannot fund a river of clones, because every key needs its own roughly six CPU-hours, about two dollars of cloud rent, plus quartz-clock time that cannot be bought in bulk.
